newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German spy chief Wolf denies Cold War crimes.
newsitem.headline: East German spy chief Wolf denies Cold War crimes.

text.p: Former East German spymaster Markus Wolf said at the start of his trial for abduction, coercion and causing bodily harm that he was not guilty because he had been serving his country.

"Neither the constitution nor the laws of the country I served were violated," Wolf told a state court in Duesseldorf. The 73-year-old Wolf said prosecutors were trying to put him into the same category as an ordinary criminal.
The trial is a last bid by prosecutors to bring Wolf to book after Germany's constitutional court in 1995 overturned a 1993 conviction for treason.
The supreme court said he could not be convicted for spying from East Berlin on what was then a foreign country -- West Germany.

This time prosecutors have charged the suave 73-year old with acts which were also illegal in East Germany -- abduction, coercion and causing bodily harm. The charges relate to East German intelligence operations in the 1950s and 1960s.
Wolf said this latest attempt to prosecute him was a political trial designed to bring discredit to the former leaders of defunct East Germany.
